desc: Quality-scored visual patterns and anti-patterns for producing specific, usable interfaces instead of generic AI-looking layouts, plus the specification-lens nodes that keep the product authority from going generic upstream.

nodes.title: A project rule outranks this brain
nodes.s: A rule under `.aioson/rules/` wins over every node here for the work it matches. Follow the rule and say which node it displaced. A client with their own design system is conforming to it, not defaulting.
nodes.p: project rule > brain node > skill default; create one with `aioson rule:new`
nodes.not: Applying a generic anti-slop pattern over an explicit project rule, or treating these nodes as unconditional law
nodes.warn: Precedence is not permission to ignore accessibility, contrast, or state coverage; a rule narrows the visual direction, not the usability floor.

nodes.title: Resolve the product signature before choosing the layout
nodes.s: Name the surface type, primary user decision, domain cues, content hierarchy, and one signature move before writing visual code. Layout follows intent instead of a fashionable preset.
nodes.p: visual thesis = surface + user decision + domain cue + signature move
nodes.src: AIOSON interface-design identity and design-direction contracts
nodes.not: Starting with a centered hero, a color palette, or a component library and hoping the product identity appears later
nodes.warn: A signature move must improve recognition or comprehension; arbitrary novelty is not a design system.

nodes.title: Replaceability test for generic composition and copy
nodes.s: Reject a surface that could serve any SaaS after changing only the logo, domain nouns, and accent color. Rework its composition and copy around the product's actual object, workflow, content, or environment. Treat repeated em dashes as a cadence smell: keep them for a deliberate interruption or contrast, and otherwise rewrite with shorter sentences or more precise punctuation.
nodes.p: remove the brand name and domain nouns; if the screen still looks complete, it is probably too generic; if nearby sentences repeat the same em-dash rhythm, rewrite them
nodes.not: Centered headline + two pills + abstract gradient/blob + three equal feature cards as the default opening composition, paired with copy that repeatedly joins asides or claims through em dashes
nodes.warn: Common patterns and an occasional em dash are allowed when intent gives them a specific reason. Preserve quotations, code, commands, and established brand punctuation.

nodes.title: Show meaningful product evidence in the first viewport
nodes.s: When the surface benefits from inspection, the first viewport should reveal the real product, content, object, place, person, or literal offer. Decoration cannot carry the entire visual argument.
nodes.p: first viewport = clear decision + meaningful evidence + usable primary action
nodes.src: AIOSON interface-design and premium-command-center quality gates
nodes.not: A hero made only of gradients, floating blobs, icons, empty cards, or abstract 3D decoration
nodes.warn: For genuinely non-visual products, state not_applicable rather than manufacturing a decorative mock.

nodes.title: Use containers for meaning, not card multiplication
nodes.s: A border, card, panel, or inset is justified by a semantic grouping, interaction boundary, state, or scan benefit. Use rows, dividers, whitespace, and dialogs when another card would add noise.
nodes.p: container = semantic group or interaction boundary; otherwise prefer hierarchy and whitespace
nodes.not: Cards inside cards, equal-weight card walls, and a card for every sentence or metric
nodes.warn: Operational dashboards may need many containers; vary hierarchy and preserve the primary task instead of applying a blanket ban.

nodes.title: One visual system, controlled contrast
nodes.s: Choose one active visual system and let typography, spacing, depth, color, and motion reinforce it. Distinction comes from coherent decisions, not stacking glass, neon, gradients, pills, shadows, and bento patterns together.
nodes.p: one visual system + one signature move + restrained supporting effects
nodes.src: AIOSON design-skill exclusivity and token contracts
nodes.not: Style soup: combining multiple preset aesthetics or using every fashionable effect in the same screen
nodes.warn: A selected design skill is the only active visual system unless an explicit hybrid process owns the combination.

nodes.title: Mobile is a recomposition, not a shrunken desktop
nodes.s: On small screens, re-evaluate order, density, controls, wrapping, media crops, and interaction priority. Preserve the product decision and identity, not the desktop geometry.
nodes.p: desktop hierarchy -> mobile priority order -> explicit compact states
nodes.not: Only shrinking font sizes and stacking desktop columns while leaving overflow, density, and control order unresolved
nodes.warn: Test real content at narrow widths; short placeholder copy hides layout failures.

nodes.title: States and behavior are part of visual quality
nodes.s: A polished surface includes the states that explain its behavior: loading, empty, error, disabled, focus, success, and relevant responsive or reduced-motion variants. Visual polish cannot hide an unfinished workflow.
nodes.p: screen quality = hierarchy + interaction + states + accessibility + responsive behavior
nodes.src: AIOSON agent implementation and prototype contracts
nodes.not: A static screenshot, toast, decorative interaction, or happy-path-only prototype presented as a complete interface
nodes.warn: Include only states material to the feature; do not invent backend behavior outside the approved scope.

nodes.title: Polish follows identity and causality
nodes.s: Refine motion, depth, hover, and transitions only after the user can understand what to do and what changed. Effects must explain state or reinforce the signature move, with reduced-motion behavior.
nodes.p: intent -> hierarchy -> real behavior -> states -> restrained polish
nodes.src: AIOSON design and implementation quality gates
nodes.not: Adding animation, blur, glow, or parallax to make an undifferentiated layout feel finished
nodes.warn: If removing the effect makes the interface confusing, fix hierarchy or copy before adding more effects.

nodes.title: Replaceability test for a generic specification and prose
nodes.s: Reject a PRD whose vision, capability map, or acceptance criteria still read complete after the domain nouns are removed. Rewrite them around the object, decision, and evidence this product actually owns. Also reject repeated em-dash cadence that substitutes rhythm for precise relationships; keep an em dash only for deliberate interruption or contrast and otherwise use direct sentences or more precise punctuation.
nodes.p: strip the domain nouns from Vision and CAP outcomes; if the text still reads complete, the specification is generic; scan neighboring sentences for repeated em-dash rhythm
nodes.src: AIOSON product authority and specification quality gate
nodes.not: A vision like "a modern, intuitive platform to manage X", capabilities named after screens, acceptance criteria asserting that the interface is responsive and intuitive, or prose that chains claims through repeated em dashes
nodes.warn: Specificity is not novelty: a conventional capability stated in this product's own terms passes, and invented differentiation does not. Preserve quotations, code, commands, and established brand punctuation.

nodes.title: An unresolved visual authority on a visible surface is a product gap
nodes.s: When the feature has a visible surface and neither an owned prototype nor an identity record resolves, record one explicit gap with its named route: extract an identity record, run a visual exploration, or accept intent-first origination with declared anti-goals.
nodes.p: visible surface + prototype none + identity none = named gap and route, never silence
nodes.src: AIOSON prototype and identity binding contracts
nodes.not: Approving a PRD whose visual contract is empty and letting implementation invent a direction to fill it
nodes.warn: Record the constraint and the route, never the composition; layout, tokens, and components stay with the prototype and the design engine.

nodes.title: Surface constraints become acceptance criteria, not prose
nodes.s: Turn the material states, asset availability, reduced-motion, performance, and accessibility expectations the surface depends on into observable acceptance rows. A constraint that lives only in a paragraph has no evidence and does not survive to QA.
nodes.p: state / asset / motion / performance constraint -> one observable AC row plus how QA proves it
nodes.not: Writing "must be fast, accessible and polished" in the PRD body while the acceptance criteria only cover the happy path
nodes.warn: Include only constraints material to this feature; do not manufacture non-functional criteria the product cannot observe.
